calls.title: Jennifer Pham-Le and Vaibhav Patel A S
calls.summary: A meeting was held to discuss the recording and backdating of a contractor payment for 2025, focusing on the manual backdating of payroll due to system limitations. calls.title: Jennifer Pham-Le and Scout Henderson
calls.summary: The session detailed the process for automated employee onboarding in the UK under EOR, emphasizing statutory requirements for vacation, attendance, and pension contributions, which start on the employee’s first day with no eligibility delays. It outlined that while employers can exceed the minimum pension contributions, they must adhere to the 3% legal minimum and employees can opt out through HR. About half of UK employers offer fully employer-funded private health insurance, with Allianz and BUPA as prominent providers. The automatic PTO setup includes 20 days plus bank holidays, with unused days not rolling over. Lastly, it confirmed that the employee is ready for payroll, having completed the necessary banking and tax information, and highlighted ongoing support for policy management and compliance.
calls.keywords: EOR, UK pension, benefits setup, PTO policy, Rippling payroll, time off approval

Jennifer and Katie discussed the Labor Portage and Consultant models, weighing their compliance and security implications. The Labor Portage model is advised for legality, featuring a 36-month maximum contract with a cooling-off period, while the Consultant model offers more flexibility but less client control. Additionally, employee onboarding support was emphasized, with Katie providing resources to streamline the hiring process and remain available for assistance.

calls.title: Jennifer Pham-Le and Katie Jones
calls.summary: The discussion focused on addressing confusion related to the visibility of variable commissions in employee contracts, specifically how they appear in offer letters. Jennifer and Katie highlighted that while the commission is indicated in employee profiles, it is not clearly documented in offer letters, leading to employee inquiries. They discussed the differences between French EOR contracts—which often include variable pay in separate addendums—and UK contracts where it is bundled. Additionally, the meeting provided insights on the Labor Portage model, emphasizing its 36-month limitation, severance pay, and conditions for extending contracts. Furthermore, the implications of the Consultant model were reviewed, which offers more flexibility but incurs higher termination costs. Legal considerations regarding contract amendments were addressed, and steps for improving contract clarity were outlined.

calls.title: Jennifer Pham-Le and Katie Jones
calls.summary: The team addressed essential issues regarding contract signing to enable benefits setup in France, clarifying that the new agreement nullifies the old one, as confirmed by Katie Jones. They also distinguished between employee agreements and Rippling's service contracts, ensuring accurate documentation for portage arrangements. Compliance requirements for time tracking in Spain include mandatory tracking with restrictions on daily work hours and managed overtime, while in France, employees submit monthly timesheets without needing managerial approval. Payroll processes were outlined, indicating that salaried payroll runs without hour approvals, while overtime is contingent on approved hours in Spain. Benefits setup for Spain is optional, while France's benefits are tied to labor portage requirements. Finally, PTO policies adhere to statutory minimums, and a commitment to ongoing support and documentation was made.
calls.keywords: employee agreement, time tracking, Spain labor law, France labor portage, benefits setup, overtime policy

calls.title: Jennifer Pham-Le and Katie Jones
calls.summary:
# Jennifer Pham-Le and Katie Jones
Date: 2026-08-24 | Duration: 11m

## Summary
The discussion clarified the flexibility of the work from home allowance of €40, which can be used for expenses like Internet or home office supplies but is not mandatory. Employees are required to submit reimbursements through Rippling’s Spend app to ensure compliance, with managers having the ability to set approval workflows. The process for reimbursing laptops was confirmed, though such reimbursements will not reflect in payroll. Payroll transition details were provided, indicating that support will shift to the client after the first payroll, with a communication sent to assist this change. Commissions will be entered directly into the payroll system, simplifying the process. Lastly, it was highlighted that the work from home allowance applies only in France, ensuring regional compliance.

## Keywords
work from home allowance, reimbursement process, Spend app, Rippling payroll, laptop reimbursement, email spam issue
